items.headline: Russell Westbrook Announces Retirement After 18 Seasons
items.summary: Nine-time All-Star and 2017 MVP Russell Westbrook officially announced his retirement from the NBA today after an illustrious 18-season career. The league's all-time leader in triple-doubles (209) shared his decision via a video narrated by Michael B. Jordan. Westbrook, who last played for the SAC Kings, was a two-time scoring champion and Olympic gold medalist.

items.headline: 2026-27 NBA Schedule Revealed, Highlighting Major Returns and New Eras
items.summary: The full 2026-27 NBA regular season schedule was released today, setting the stage for highly anticipated matchups. The season will tip off on October 20 with a tripleheader, including LeBron James and Jaylen Brown's new-look PHI 76ers visiting the reigning champion NYK Knicks, who will receive their rings. Other notable games include Jaylen Brown's return to BOS on Jan. 21 after his trade to PHI, and Giannis Antetokounmpo's return to MIL on Jan. 28 with his new MIA Heat squad.

items.headline: Los Angeles Lakers Reportedly Selling for Record $12.5 Billion
items.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers are reportedly being sold to former Disney CEO Bob Iger and investor Joshua Kushner in a deal valued at a staggering $12.5 billion, according to ESPN. This record-breaking valuation for a North American sports franchise is pending approval from the NBA's board of governors.

items.headline: Several Teams Still Have Open Two-Way Contract Spots
items.summary: As the offseason progresses, 14 NBA teams currently have at least one open two-way contract spot for the upcoming 2026-27 season. The NYK Knicks are the only team with all three two-way slots available, while the DEN Nuggets have two. Expected signings include Jalen Pickett to the LAC Clippers, Carson Cooper to the MEM Grizzlies, and Rafael Castro to the MIL Bucks. Two-way players will earn $678,882 in 2026-27 and are eligible for up to 50 regular season games.
